examples.text: Пора убрать все старые вещи отсюда.
examples.trans: It is time to remove all the old things from here.

examples.text: Да уйду я, только свои вещи заберу.
examples.trans: Yes, I will leave, I will just pick up my things.

examples.text: Я тебе вещи привезла.
examples.trans: I've brought you your things.

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will take', paired with 'забирать'.

examples.text: Ты решил забрать мою работу, старый друг?
examples.trans: Did you decide to take my job, old friend?

examples.text: Он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: He will withdraw the statement.

examples.text: Я заберу ключи.
examples.trans: I'll take the keys.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Виктория Сергеевна, я сразу не заметил.
examples.trans: Viktoria Sergeyevna, I did not notice right away.

examples.text: Пойдёмте, Виктория Сергеевна, выпьем кофе.
examples.trans: Let us go, Viktoria Sergeyevna, and drink coffee.

examples.text: Виктор, как я рад тебя видеть!
examples.trans: Viktor, how glad I am to see you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это очень смешно, Дмитрий Владимирович.
examples.trans: That is very funny, Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Да, это было давно в армии.
examples.trans: Yes, that was a long time ago in the army.

examples.text: Это мой старый друг из Парижа.
examples.trans: This is my old friend from Paris.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Подожди, кто это там стоит на кухне?
examples.trans: Wait, who is that standing in the kitchen over there?

examples.text: Там всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine there.

examples.text: Кто там?
examples.trans: Who's there?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is standing', paired with 'постоять'.

examples.text: Это просто настоящий праздник для меня, друг!
examples.trans: This is simply a real holiday for me, friend!

examples.text: Я стою здесь.
examples.trans: I'm standing here.

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cook' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Быстро за работу, повара!
examples.trans: Quickly back to work, cooks!

examples.text: Дима, поверь мне, я в полном порядке.
examples.trans: Dima, believe me, I am completely fine.

examples.text: Можно сейчас пригласить сюда повара Катю?
examples.trans: May we invite the cook Katya here right now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Сейчас ваш шеф сам готовить будет!
examples.trans: Right now your chef is going to cook himself!

examples.text: Почему он решил готовить до ужина?
examples.trans: Why did he decide to cook before dinner?

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, шеф сам для вас готовит.
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, the chef is cooking for you himself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Для него это очень скучное место.
examples.trans: For him this is a very boring place.

examples.text: Вот новый заказ для Дмитрия Владимировича.
examples.trans: Here is a new order for Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, шеф сам для вас готовит.
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, the chef is cooking for you himself.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guests' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тебя в зале спрашивает гость.
examples.trans: A guest is asking for you in the dining room.

examples.text: Французский гость, наверное, уже выдал меня.
examples.trans: The French guest probably already gave me away.

examples.text: Катя, что сейчас говорит этот гость?
examples.trans: Katya, what is this guest saying right now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф уже два месяца обещает меню.
examples.trans: The chef has been promising a menu for two months already.

examples.text: Уже два часа дня на улице!
examples.trans: It is already two o'clock in the afternoon outside!

examples.text: Ладно, я возьму только два дня.
examples.trans: Alright, I will take only two days.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'beef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Повара готовят для гостей две говядины.
examples.trans: The cooks are preparing two beef dishes for the guests.

examples.text: Говядина, печень.
examples.trans: Beef, liver.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Почему ты кричишь на весь ресторан?
examples.trans: Why are you shouting across the whole restaurant?

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

examples.text: Как вы все знаете...
examples.trans: As you all know...

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'say, speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Катя, что сейчас говорит этот гость?
examples.trans: Katya, what is this guest saying right now?

examples.text: Говорит, что ему здесь не нравится.
examples.trans: He says that he does not like it here.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не говорите отцу про меня.
examples.trans: Please do not tell my father about me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to him', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Рождаются миллионы новых людей.
examples.trans: Millions of new people are born.

examples.text: Ведь уже скоро лето закончится.
examples.trans: After all, summer will end soon.

examples.text: Макс, откуда он здесь взялся?
examples.trans: Max, where did he come from here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'took', paired with 'занимать'.

examples.text: Кто занял моё место?
examples.trans: Who took my place?

examples.text: Не успел я уйти, ты занял моё место?
examples.trans: Before I even had time to leave, you took my place?

examples.text: Займите тогда хотя бы денег.
examples.trans: Then lend me at least some money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это мой старый друг из Парижа.
examples.trans: This is my old friend from Paris.

examples.text: Шеф, это точно не мой ребёнок!
examples.trans: Chef, this is definitely not my child!

examples.text: Иди домой, Витя, до вечера!
examples.trans: Go home, Vitya, until tonight!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'place' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Шеф уже два месяца обещает меню.
examples.trans: The chef has been promising a menu for two months already.

examples.text: Мы раньше долго работали вместе.
examples.trans: We used to work together for a long time.

examples.text: Для него это очень скучное место.
examples.trans: For him this is a very boring place.
